title: The four-point converse: orthogonal diagonals, scaling, and cap bases

blocks.tex: The four-point base is an explicit positive orthogonal quadrilateral. Its axis lengths solve the four curvature equations; the retained identities also supply the anchor rank calculations.

blocks.label: def:n4c_four_profile
blocks.title: four-point profile
blocks.body:
For $x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3\in\mathbb{R}$, $\mathrm{fourProfile}(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)$
  is the function $\ZMod 4\to\mathbb{R}$ sending $i$ to $x_{i}$, read through
  the canonical representative $i.\mathrm{val}\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.fourProfile
lean.code:
def fourProfile (x₀ x₁ x₂ x₃ : ℝ) : ZMod 4 → ℝ := fun i =>
  ![x₀, x₁, x₂, x₃] ⟨i.val, i.val_lt⟩

blocks.label: def:n4c_orthogonal_quad
blocks.title: orthogonal-diagonal quadrilateral
blocks.body:
For $a,b,c,d>0$ let $\mathrm{orthogonalQuad}(a,b,c,d):\ZMod 4\to\mathbb{C}$
  be the vertex map
  \[
    0\mapsto a,\qquad 1\mapsto b\,i,\qquad 2\mapsto -c,\qquad 3\mapsto -d\,i .
  \]
  Its two diagonals are the segments $[-c,a]$ of the real axis and
  $[-d\,i,b\,i]$ of the imaginary axis, so they meet orthogonally at the
  origin, and $a,b,c,d$ are the four half-diagonals.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalQuad
lean.code:
def orthogonalQuad (a b c d : ℝ) : ZMod 4 → ℂ := fun i =>
  ![(a : ℂ), (b : ℂ) * Complex.I, -(c : ℂ), -(d : ℂ) * Complex.I]
    ⟨i.val, i.val_lt⟩

blocks.label: lem:n4c_quad_simple
blocks.title: the orthogonal quadrilateral is simple
blocks.body:
For $a,b,c,d>0$ the polygon $\mathrm{orthogonalQuad}(a,b,c,d)$ is simple:
  consecutive vertices are distinct, consecutive closed edges meet exactly in
  their shared vertex, and non-adjacent closed edges are disjoint.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.isSimplePolygon_orthogonalQuad
lean.code:
theorem isSimplePolygon_orthogonalQuad {a b c d : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d) :
    IsSimplePolygon (orthogonalQuad a b c d) :=
  ⟨orthogonalQuad_edge_ne ha hb hc hd,
    orthogonalQuad_consecutive_inter ha hb hc hd,
    orthogonalQuad_nonadjacent_disjoint ha hb hc hd⟩

blocks.tex:
Each closed edge is a segment with one endpoint on the real axis and one on
  the imaginary axis, so a point $z$ of the edge from $x\in\mathbb{R}$ to
  $y\,i$ has $\Re z = r x$ and $\Im z = s y$ with $r,s\ge 0$, $r+s=1$.  Two
  such segments sharing an axis endpoint but with opposite-sign partners meet
  only in that endpoint: if the two real endpoints $x_+ > 0 > x_-$ are
  opposite in sign, then $\Re z\ge 0$ from one description and $\Re z\le 0$
  from the other, forcing $\Re z = 0$ and hence the coefficient of the real
  endpoint to vanish in each; the same argument with the roles of the axes
  exchanged handles a shared imaginary endpoint.  For the two non-adjacent
  pairs, the same coordinate reading forces $\Re z = \Im z = 0$, i.e.\ $z=0$,
  and $0$ lies on no edge because $r+s=1$ makes at least one of $rx$, $sy$
  nonzero.  Distinctness of consecutive vertices is immediate from
  positivity.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_realizes_menger_orthogonal
blocks.title: curvature of the orthogonal quadrilateral
blocks.body:
Let $a,b,c,d>0$ and $A,B,C,D>0$ satisfy the four Pythagorean relations
  \[
    A^2=a^2+b^2,\quad B^2=b^2+c^2,\quad C^2=c^2+d^2,\quad D^2=d^2+a^2 ,
  \]
  and put
  \[
    \kappa_0=\frac{2a}{AD},\quad \kappa_1=\frac{2b}{AB},\quad
    \kappa_2=\frac{2c}{BC},\quad \kappa_3=\frac{2d}{CD} .
  \]
  Then $\mathrm{RealizesMenger}\,\mathrm{fourProfile}(\kappa_0,\dots,\kappa_3)$,
  witnessed by $\mathrm{orthogonalQuad}(a,b,c,d)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesMenger_fourProfile_of_orthogonal
lean.code:
theorem realizesMenger_fourProfile_of_orthogonal
    {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ a b c d A B C D : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hA : 0 < A) (hB : 0 < B) (hC : 0 < C) (hD : 0 < D)
    (hAsq : A ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) (hBsq : B ^ 2 = b ^ 2 + c ^ 2)
    (hCsq : C ^ 2 = c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) (hDsq : D ^ 2 = d ^ 2 + a ^ 2)
    (hk₀ : 2 * a / (A * D) = k₀) (hk₁ : 2 * b / (A * B) = k₁)
    (hk₂ : 2 * c / (B * C) = k₂) (hk₃ : 2 * d / (C * D) = k₃) :
    RealizesMenger (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) := by
  refine ⟨orthogonalQuad a b c d, isSimplePolygon_orthogonalQuad ha hb hc hd, ?_⟩
  intro i
  rcases zmod4_cases i with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 3) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 0)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 1) = k₀
    rw [orthogonalQuad_three, orthogonalQuad_zero, orthogonalQuad_one,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_zero ha hb hd hA hD hAsq (by nlinarith), hk₀]
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 0) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 1)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 2) = k₁
    rw [orthogonalQuad_zero, orthogonalQuad_one, orthogonalQuad_two,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_one ha hb hc hA hB hAsq hBsq, hk₁]
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 1) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 2)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 3) = k₂
    rw [orthogonalQuad_one, orthogonalQuad_two, orthogonalQuad_three,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_two hb hc hd hB hC hBsq hCsq, hk₂]
  · change signedMengerR2 (orthogonalQuad a b c d 2) (orthogonalQuad a b c d 3)
        (orthogonalQuad a b c d 0) = k₃
    rw [orthogonalQuad_two, orthogonalQuad_three, orthogonalQuad_zero,
      signedMenger_orthogonal_three ha hc hd hC hD hCsq hDsq, hk₃]

blocks.tex:
By \cref{lem:n4c_quad_simple} the quadrilateral is simple, so only the four
  curvature values must be checked, one per residue.  The distance between a
  real point $x$ and an imaginary point $y\,i$ is $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$; under the
  four Pythagorean hypotheses the six pairwise distances among consecutive
  triples are exactly $A,B,C,D$ and the two diagonals $a+c$, $b+d$.  At vertex
  $0$ the triple is $(-d\,i,\;a,\;b\,i)$; its two adjacent side lengths are
  $D$ and $A$, and twice the signed area of the triangle is $2a(b+d)/2$, so
  the signed Menger curvature is $2a/(AD)$.  The three remaining residues are
  the same computation with the labels rotated.

The four curvature equations of \cref{lem:n4c_realizes_menger_orthogonal} are
solved by an exact rational formula for the \emph{squared} side lengths.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalDelta
lean.code:
def orthogonalDelta (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  k₀ ^ 2 * k₂ ^ 2 - k₁ ^ 2 * k₃ ^ 2

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalA2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalA2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₂ ^ 2 - k₃ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalB2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalB2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₀ ^ 2 - k₃ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalC2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalC2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₀ ^ 2 - k₁ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalD2
lean.code:
noncomputable def orthogonalD2 (k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  4 * (k₂ ^ 2 - k₁ ^ 2) / orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃

blocks.tex:
The four Pythagorean relations then hold \emph{identically} in the
$\kappa_i$; no positivity is needed, only $\Delta\ne 0$.  In each case the
common factor cancels and what remains is one two-term telescoping of
$\Delta = \kappa_0^2\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2\kappa_3^2$.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityA
blocks.title: first Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal A = \tfrac14\kappa_0^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal D
     + \tfrac14\kappa_1^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal B$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalA2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalA2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₀ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₁ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalA2 orthogonalB2 orthogonalD2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.tex:
Clearing denominators and cancelling the common factor
  $4(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_3^2)/\Delta$ reduces the claim to
  $\kappa_0^2(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2)+\kappa_1^2(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_3^2) = \Delta$,
  i.e.\ to
  $\kappa_0^2\kappa_2^2-\kappa_0^2\kappa_1^2
   +\kappa_0^2\kappa_1^2-\kappa_1^2\kappa_3^2
   = \kappa_0^2\kappa_2^2-\kappa_1^2\kappa_3^2$.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityB
blocks.title: second Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal B = \tfrac14\kappa_1^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal B
     + \tfrac14\kappa_2^2\,\mathcal B\mathcal C$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalB2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalB2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₁ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₂ ^ 2 * orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalA2 orthogonalB2 orthogonalC2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.tex:
Cancelling $4(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_3^2)/\Delta$ leaves
  $\kappa_1^2(\kappa_2^2-\kappa_3^2)+\kappa_2^2(\kappa_0^2-\kappa_1^2) = \Delta$,
  again a telescoping in $\kappa_1^2\kappa_2^2$.

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityC
blocks.title: third Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal C = \tfrac14\kappa_2^2\,\mathcal B\mathcal C
     + \tfrac14\kappa_3^2\,\mathcal C\mathcal D$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalC2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalC2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₂ ^ 2 * orthogonalB2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₃ ^ 2 * orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalB2 orthogonalC2 orthogonalD2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.label: lem:n4c_identityD
blocks.title: fourth Pythagorean identity
blocks.body:
If $\Delta\ne 0$ then
  $\mathcal D = \tfrac14\kappa_3^2\,\mathcal C\mathcal D
     + \tfrac14\kappa_0^2\,\mathcal A\mathcal D$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonalD2_identity
lean.code:
lemma orthogonalD2_identity {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : orthogonalDelta k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ ≠ 0) :
    orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ =
      k₃ ^ 2 * orthogonalC2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 +
        k₀ ^ 2 * orthogonalA2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ *
          orthogonalD2 k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ / 4 := by
  unfold orthogonalA2 orthogonalC2 orthogonalD2
  field_simp [hΔ]
  unfold orthogonalDelta
  ring

blocks.tex:
\texttt{RealizesMenger} records a simple polygon with the right curvatures.
The project's realizability predicate $\mathrm{RealizesR2}$ asks for more: a
positive edge-length vector satisfying every strict arcsine \emph{moderate
wall}, closing, with total turn exactly $2\pi$, and with simple development.
The orthogonal quadrilateral supplies all four at once.

blocks.label: thm:n4c_realization_data
blocks.title: the orthogonal quadrilateral is a moderate development
blocks.body:
Under the hypotheses of \cref{lem:n4c_realizes_menger_orthogonal}, the
  length vector $\ell=\mathrm{fourProfile}(A,B,C,D)$ satisfies
  \[
    \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell,\qquad
    \mathrm{closureGap}\,\kappa\,\ell = 0,\qquad
    \mathrm{turningSum}\,\kappa\,\ell = 2\pi,
  \]
  and the development $\mathrm{polygonR2}\,\kappa\,\ell$ is simple.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.orthogonal_realization_data
lean.code:
theorem orthogonal_realization_data
    {k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃ a b c d A B C D : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hA : 0 < A) (hB : 0 < B) (hC : 0 < C) (hD : 0 < D)
    (hAsq : A ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) (hBsq : B ^ 2 = b ^ 2 + c ^ 2)
    (hCsq : C ^ 2 = c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) (hDsq : D ^ 2 = d ^ 2 + a ^ 2)
    (hk₀ : 2 * a / (A * D) = k₀) (hk₁ : 2 * b / (A * B) = k₁)
    (hk₂ : 2 * c / (B * C) = k₂) (hk₃ : 2 * d / (C * D) = k₃) :
    ModerateArc 0 (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D) ∧
      closureGap (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D) = 0 ∧
      turningSum (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D) =
        2 * Real.pi ∧
      IsSimplePolygon
        (polygonR2 (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) (fourProfile A B C D)) := by
  let ℓ : ZMod 4 → ℝ := fourProfile A B C D
  have hk₀pos : 0 < k₀ := by rw [← hk₀]; positivity
  have hk₁pos : 0 < k₁ := by rw [← hk₁]; positivity
  have hk₂pos : 0 < k₂ := by rw [← hk₂]; positivity
  have hk₃pos : 0 < k₃ := by rw [← hk₃]; positivity
  have haA : a < A := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hb]
  have hbA : b < A := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos ha]
  have hbB : b < B := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hc]
  have hcB : c < B := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hb]
  have hcC : c < C := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hd]
  have hdC : d < C := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hc]
  have hdD : d < D := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos ha]
  have haD : a < D := by nlinarith [sq_pos_of_pos hd]
  have hMA : ModerateArc 0 (fourProfile k₀ k₁ k₂ k₃) ℓ := by
    rw [moderateArc_zero_iff]
    intro i
    rcases zmod4_cases i with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_zero]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₀pos, ← hk₀]
      refine ⟨hA, ?_, ?_⟩
      · calc
          2 * a / (A * D) * (D / 2) = a / A := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hA).2 haA
      · calc
          2 * a / (A * D) * (A / 2) = a / D := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hD).2 haD
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_one]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₁pos, ← hk₁]
      refine ⟨hB, ?_, ?_⟩
      · calc
          2 * b / (A * B) * (A / 2) = b / B := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hB).2 hbB
      · calc
          2 * b / (A * B) * (B / 2) = b / A := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hA).2 hbA
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_two]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₂pos, ← hk₂]
      refine ⟨hC, ?_, ?_⟩
      · calc
          2 * c / (B * C) * (B / 2) = c / C := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hC).2 hcC
      · calc
          2 * c / (B * C) * (C / 2) = c / B := by field_simp
          _ < 1 := (div_lt_one hB).2 hcB
    · simp only [ℓ, fourProfile_three]
      rw [abs_of_pos hk₃pos, ← hk₃]
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Write the four turns.  By definition
  $\theta_i = \arcsin(\kappa_i\ell_{i-1}/2) + \arcsin(\kappa_i\ell_i/2)$, and
  with $\kappa_0=2a/(AD)$, $\ell_3=D$, $\ell_0=A$ we get
  $\kappa_0\ell_3/2 = a/A$ and $\kappa_0\ell_0/2 = a/D$; cyclically,
  \[
    \theta_0 = \arcsin\tfrac aA + \arcsin\tfrac aD,\quad
    \theta_1 = \arcsin\tfrac bA + \arcsin\tfrac bB,\quad
    \theta_2 = \arcsin\tfrac cB + \arcsin\tfrac cC,\quad
    \theta_3 = \arcsin\tfrac dC + \arcsin\tfrac dD .
  \]
  \emph{Walls.}  Each Pythagorean relation makes a leg strictly shorter than
  its hypotenuse ($a<A$ because $b>0$, and so on), so every argument above
  lies strictly inside $(0,1)$ and each moderate wall is strict.

  \emph{Turn sum.}  The key elementary identity is
  \[
    h^2 = x^2+y^2,\ x,y,h>0
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \arcsin\tfrac xh + \arcsin\tfrac yh = \tfrac\pi2 ,
  \]
  which holds because $\sqrt{1-(x/h)^2} = y/h$ turns
  $\arccos(x/h)$ into $\arcsin(y/h)$, and
  $\arccos = \pi/2 - \arcsin$.  Regrouping the eight arcsines by
  \emph{hypotenuse} rather than by vertex,
  \[
    \sum_i\theta_i
    = \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac aA+\arcsin\tfrac bA\Bigr)
    + \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac bB+\arcsin\tfrac cB\Bigr)
    + \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac cC+\arcsin\tfrac dC\Bigr)
    + \Bigl(\arcsin\tfrac dD+\arcsin\tfrac aD\Bigr)
    = 4\cdot\tfrac\pi2 = 2\pi .
  \]
  This is the polygon's four right angles at the diagonal crossing, read
  through the development.

  \emph{Closure.}  The same identity, in exponential form,
  $e^{\,i\arcsin(x/h)} = y/h + i\,x/h$, evaluates each developed direction:
  there is one global unit phase $\rho$ with
  $e^{\,i\psi_0}=\rho u_0$, \dots, $e^{\,i\psi_3}=\rho u_3$, where $u_0,\dots,u_3$
  are the four explicit unit vectors
  $(-a+ib)/A$, $(-c-ib)/B$, $(c-id)/C$, $(a+id)/D$ --- the normalized side
  vectors of the quadrilateral.  Then
  $A u_0 + B u_1 + C u_2 + D u_3 = (-a+ib)+(-c-ib)+(c-id)+(a+id) = 0$,
  so $\mathrm{closureGap} = \rho\cdot 0 = 0$.

  \emph{Simplicity.}  All four turns are positive and sum to $2\pi$, so the
  development is convex, hence simple (\cref{thm:convex_simple}).
